title: I focussed on giving the best premarket user experience ever.
author: KimOnMacro
selftext:
Hey AI Traders, Kim here.  
  
Right now before a trade you check the news. Maybe ask chatgpt or google ai.   
Might go on X, or even looking at COT reports if you're diligent (or even prompting that too!)  
  
I built EchelonEdgeAI to make all of that a million times better:  
  
**More accurate.** I'm currently paying for real data feeds (Financial Modelling Prep) and also adding in free but institutional data feeds (FRED/EIA) to feed my AI. Things like real yields, live pricing, indexes etc.   
  
**More convenient.** No prompting, no typing a question and hoping you asked it right. Pick your asset or flip the swing toggle. That's it. The answer also doesnt change unless theres new data to debate that (Compared to AI's that keep changing their mind even if you ask the same q twice)  
  
**More intelligent.** It's not just answering the one thing you thought to ask. It's tracing the kind of chain most people wouldn't think to follow. E.g:  
Copper mine disruption → chip production slows → tech stocks take a hit → NAS100 drags with it.   
Iran tensions → oil supply risk → USDCAD moves.   
That's the stuff sitting three steps away from the obvious headline, connected automatically.  
  
**Faster.** Live X feeds can be the fastest source of news especially from accounts like Financial Juice or Unusual Whales. (Currently refreshing every 15-30 min while I'm keeping API costs sane in free beta, that'll get much tighter once it's paid) Being upfront: not instant yet, just faster than checking five accounts yourself.  
  
**More in the loop.** Actual CFTC COT data displayed super cleanly. Where hedge funds and institutions are actually positioned right now. So you dont trade against them.  
  
Then it collapses all of that into one summary.   
  
Free to use right now.  
  
I'm planning to move to paid pricing eventually, though genuinely open to pushing that back if people are getting real value and want more time. If you want to try it, drop a comment and I'll send it over. Would love feedback either way.   
  
Interesting? Good? Bad? Didnt feel much value? Anything you feel would be amazing guys.

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body:
I'm trying to see how this would be useful.   
And associating LLM with intelligence is already spooking me out especially when money and life is involved. I am also curious (in a bad way) what rational/reasoning your LLM would use to make predictions. As a general rule of thumb in developer world, LLM enhances automation never involve decision making process. 

The only potential usefulness I might see is that if you have a platform that could extract live data and organize it in simplified ergonomic fashion so I don't have to click multiple times to get raw data from various different sources... kinda like hosting a buffet instead of going to 5 different restaurants to try  different cuisines. But even in this case, so many questions are brought up like why use LLM if pathways are finite and relatively small variance wise and risk hallucination or other unexpected output unnecessarily? 

IMHO in modern times like this, getting the information fast isn't really a great moat as information becomes easier and faster for everyone to get. The bigger prize is establishing sufficient context and acumen in the field to better analyze immense data by filtering out what is important and what is not  and how to refine it into an algo or some system that produces useful output. 

I dunno some 2cents when glancing at the post

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Hey! Really appreciate this question, genuinely!   
  
To be clear on where the AI actually sits: it's not making the trade call. The verdict logic (COT positioning, how a release affects an asset) is deterministic, rule based, not the LLM reasoning its way to a decision. The AI's job is narrower, pulling in live news and organizing it, closer to what you called it, a buffet instead of five restaurants! (great analogy, btw)

On hallucination risk, that's why the numbers (COT, yields, pricing) come from real paid APIs, not the model guessing or remembering a value.

Your last point is the one I don't have a clean answer to. Raw info speed isn't much of a moat anymore, you're right. The one part is that most traders don't have years of context to know which cross market connections even matter, like a copper disruption hitting NAS100. That's what I'm trying to surface, not " just faster info" but "the connection you wouldn't have thought to check, checked fast" Whether that's enough long term is fair to be skeptical about, and I'd rather hear that now

replies.author: silphotographer
replies.body:
Despite what the media says, world current events do not necessarily correlate to the price action. You've heard so many sob stories about angry retails who says the news was good so why is price going the wrong way the market is rigged etc etc. There are a lot of moving parts... current events are merely one factor and even in that realm, there may be competing current events. Sometimes institutional direction outweighs current events. 

Do not take everything I say and take it with grain of salt ofc as I got no skin in the game (and as you know everyone's got opinions means little until you take position), but if I had to share something I would say perhaps the useful niche LLM is maybe training the LLM agent with enough valid and  relevant context so that it can think like you would (except the decision would be much faster and decisive). Despite hallucination risk, if the agent is well trained enough... and if LLM can provide simplified TLDR summary of all the process with ok/cancel option you can skim through it and say yeah this seems good enough or if it looks funny you have an option to bail and reassess. 

But this is complicated af for so many reasons. One: have fun trying to find real competent traders with solid track record and street cred to become your AI agent data feeder. Most wouldn't be interested in sharing their process and even if they do for some reason I imagine it'd be hefty price wise. Secondly, your audience is gonna be diverse... with their own processes, contexts, priorities, etc.

Only way to resolve  that I think is to come up with some process that will interact with the audience and gather enough useful context/data so  that the AI agent would mimic the user and how they come up with decision making process (won't be perfect but good enough to be useful).  But that also comes with challenges like:

1. Most retail traders don't know wtf they are doing. They love intellectual masturbation about trading discipline and mindset when they never even bothered to see if their trading system actually has statistical edge (ex. it's like when a driver is saying hey I'm gonna train really hard to be a great driver when their car is totally wrecked). A losing system can be perfectly executed and it'd still be a loss.   
2. How many retail traders would be patient and cooperative enough to follow through exhaustive and demanding input demands from the LLM to do its magic? Imagine an online  dating website that tries to max the matching process by gathering as much info about you as possible. Great in theory, but most users would just delete the app if it takes like half an hour or more  to set up profiling. That's not LLM's fault... just bad user interface/ergonomics

  
Maybe one potential idea that might work (no clue how it would work) is create some LLM that can interact with the real market data/historic data so that  if the user provides some trading idea, the LLM can do basic  shit test/stress  test to see if there is a potential correlation to success (not guaranteed ofc). That may force retail traders to  at least rule out bad trading ideas (like FVG concept that is catching popularity). 

I'm rambling now gonna stop before I go really off topic but these are my train of thoughts on this topic.



IMHO I'd go back to business 101: if you wanna find a successful business, talk to your potential customers and find out what problems/pain points they struggle with enough to consider paying a premium if you have a solution. Maybe talk to average to below average retail traders/civilians and see what would help them enough to pay subscription fee. 

Having said that I wouldn't crush your idea. Plenty of pirate websites are out there to stream tv shows and movies for free, but there are plenty of Netflix customers for a reason. Maybe your platform could be like Netflix if it's set up good. But even in that aspiration to build buffet instead of individual restaurant, then you gotta find out... what do your  usual customers often have to hassle information wise? How would  they be displayed interface wise where your customer would say wow that's nice I don't need million windows how I like to see information is all neatly organized in a way that helps me click faster or process easier. 

Hope you have Steve Job like intuition... and that's saying something as I'm phobic to Apple company  lol even if I  do respect some elements.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Firstly, absolutely loved hearing those thoughts! You said you were rambling but thats exactly what I wanted to hear to see how different traders react or think to this. 

You're completely right that a single news doesn't reliably correlate to price on its own, and institutional positioning can absolutely override it, that's the exact thing that got me into building this in the first place, watching a clean technical setup get wrecked by something price action alone never would've told me. That's actually closer to what I'm going for than what came across in my post(?) The app isn't trying to predict price off news alone, it's meant to sit alongside technicals, not replace them, the fundamentals side is filling in the "why did this just move against me" gap, not generating the entry itself. I've also got down in my app a how to use section showing the entry works much better when both technicals and fundamental/macro stories align perfectly! 

Your point about training an agent on how an actual trader thinks is super interesting, and you're right about why it's hard. Good traders don't want to hand over their process, and even if they did, everyone's process is different enough that one model probably wouldn't generalize well across users anyway. Esp when psychology is all over the show for differnt ppl. That's a much harder, longer term problem than what I'm solving right now, but it's a good one to sit with.

The exhaustive input/profiling concern I think applies more to that specific idea though, not to what's actually built. If the goal was training something to mimic each individual trader's personal process, yeah, that'd need a ton of upfront input, and you're right most people would bail before finishing it, same as your dating app comparison. What I've built goes the opposite direction on purpose, pick your asset, done, verdict loads in a few seconds. No setup, no profiling, nothing to fill out. That was intentional, I think most trading tools ask too much before they've earned it, you should see if something's useful before you invest ten minutes setting it up.

Your Netflix/buffet point is the one I want to actually build toward harder! You're right that the win isn't just having the data, it's making someone go "I don't need five windows open, this is just so clean." That's genuinely the bar I'm trying to hit on the UI side, less like a terminal, more like something you'd actually want to open first thing before a session instead of tolerating because it has the data you need (so visuals and clarity wise, I hope Ive hit that feeling. But still absolutely will work on fine tuning as with everyones ideas they share with me!) 

The stress test idea, feeding in a trading idea and checking it against historical correlation, is genuinely good too (and actually could work as the data provider I pay does provider historical values too), and honestly probably closer to something worth building toward than what exists in the app today. Appreciate you thinking this far into it instead of just dismissing the whole premise.

comments.author: qqAzo
comments.body:
There is a saying - trade the rumour sell the news. How do you ensure your model doesn't give the most bullish sign when the news come out?

As I see you basically point to the top with a news engine like this. Do you have any analysis that you actually have an edge?

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Fair challenge! And this is actually what the app builds around too!  
  
E.g. When a print comes out, if the immediate reaction goes against the broader macro bias, the verdict doesn't flip bullish on the headline, it moves to neutral for a short window instead.   
  
Partly because I can't out-react algo trading on the initial spike, and partly because that's usually exactly the kind of move that reverses once the rumor-vs-news gap closes. But if that shift actually holds, say a central bank surprises with a rate hike and yields stay elevated over the following sessions instead of fading, that's no longer treated as noise, it gets folded into the actual bias.   
  
There's also an intraday vs swing toggle, since whether a piece of news still matters depends a lot on your timeframe and you can see if that news piece weighs out in a longer TF too. Saying that, my app is definitely not for scalpers for sure!

comments.author: Then_Presence9297
comments.body:
nice, COT display alone would get me to try it tbh. doesnt the friday report only have tuesday data in it though? At monday its like a week old already, do you show the report date somewhere?

how do you get same answer to stay between runs, just cache? whenever i rerun the same inputs i get a different answer, so id love to know the trick.

the copper to NAS100 type stuff. or how do you keep the model from calling the same headline bullish one time and bearish the next? both versions always sound good.   
the dedup part is what killed me on my own thing btw, same story comes 15 times, half with wrong tickers. how do you handle that? and count me in for the beta

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Firstly thank you! And happy to answer :)

For the COT, it does have the Tue data and so i have the timestamped label on when it gets pulled its on the core metrics section of the dashboard, also on the COT page too. However, I think this is still okay for the accuracy as I am using the COT data more to weigh the swing analysis as it would fit a multi week read a lot better than intraday.

On staying consistent, you're right! I've made it so it checks against whether any of the values its watching have actually changed since last time in a meaningful way (ranges have been set). If nothing moved, nothing reruns and so same answer holds. E.g. if a new release print comes or core metrics like VIX moves enough to matter etc then it would force a refresh. And then any new news over the top would be through a delta change of whether this is enough to tip the verdict. For the headline flip thing, I pull it with enough summary context that it should tell the model whether something's bearish or bullish more reliably than a bare headline, and there's a neutral option built in for anything ambiguous (although I still pickup inaccuracies occasionally for this, so my flip isnt perfect unfortunately). If you run into it, let me know what triggered it, that'd actually help me look into it even more!!

On dedup, it's a Jaccard index similarity check so the same story with different tickers doesn't spam the input. Still tuning the edge cases, sometimes stuff slips through!! 

For the app itself, you can find it here [https://echelonedgeai.com/](https://echelonedgeai.com/)

Honest question, why would anyone pay for your thin API wrapper?

Why not just use Codex? It can do so much more. Just save a skill for this. Or have it build you a dashboard. And you can use 5.6 Sol for analysis. All for $20 per month.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Hey Fomoz, thanks for the question! (Btw don't hold back for roasts, as I really want to hear more input so I can make the product better!)

As you said, the model call itself is easy. The paying eventually would be more for everything wired around it like watching X tweets, other APIs, continous tracking, and calibrating a verdict from multiple factors and maintaining it. (although saying that, for people that want to do it for free personal use, they can use RSS feeds!)   
  
And I guess the one I feel passionately (but have not much data to prove) is that the user experience can be a lot better for every trader. Currently I see people around me trade (Actually fam swing trades lol) and so when I see them search news and constantly prompt GPT for cross market effects, current news etc, I thought why can't I make that easy to visualise, in one step without prompting? Which is what lead me here :)

And then OpenAI or Anthropic will release the same thing included in their plans and you're done. But they're almost the same now anyway, just not 100% turnkey.

replies.author: KimOnMacro

That's a fair point honestly, can't debate that. If Open AI released the same thing I'll be finished lol!   
  
I think the bet is just that big labs hopefully will develop a dedicated ux over a longer horizon and that for now, I am focussing on personally asking everyone that uses my app things that can make them feel that 1% more seamlessness during their workflow.
